A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CODE-CL and contain complete, readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original CODE-CL benchmark evaluations, resource measurements, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original CODE-CL evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix B, including accuracy, forgetting, and forward-transfer outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same task-overlap analysis, shared-direction learning, gradient projection, and conceptor updates. The model architectures and training objectives are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Split CIFAR100, Split miniImageNet, 5-Datasets, and OL-CIFAR100 with the same task coverage, including the overlapping-class scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding experiments. Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain GPM, TRGP, CUBER, SGP, and their respective additional baselines without additions or removals.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same reported architectures, data partitions, preprocessing, training budgets, hyperparameters, and ACC, BWT, and relative FWT evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The aperture and free-dimension sensitivity analyses in Figures 4–5 and the additional aperture, free-dimension, and threshold ablations in Appendix B are unchanged. The per-task and resource analyses are also retained.

E5.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4–7 retain the same five-trial, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. No run-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All reported results and plotted trends are unchanged, including the appendix ablations. For example, Table 1 retains CODE-CL accuracies of 77.21%, 71.16%, and 93.51%, and Table 4 retains 76.89% on OL-CIFAR100.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(11), Appendix A's treatment of noninvertible conceptors, and Section 4.2.2's memory-complexity derivation are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, arguments, or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating forgetting, promoting forward transfer, and improving accuracy through conceptor-based gradient projection.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of shared-direction learning and pseudo-orthogonal projection, along with the same forgetting–plasticity and performance–memory trade-offs in Section 4.2 and Appendix B.

D1.justification: v3 adds a page-1 footnote stating that code is available and providing the mapolinario94/CODE-CL GitHub repository link; v2 has no corresponding access information. Implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 37 cited works and research positioning are retained. Reference [36]'s changed citation-page listing reflects text reflow, not a removed citation or changed relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v3 adds the short code-availability footnote and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new footnote and separator on page 1 cause limited column and page reflow through page 4. Figures 1–5, Tables 1–10, and the supplementary layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides an explicit implementation location absent from v2, modestly improving code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and evidence are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or executability.
